ri_table.name: other
ri_table.source: Confirmed from the published source code (github.com/bpmsg/ahp-os, classes/AhpCalc.php): the function setAlonsoCr() computes CR = (lambda_max - n) / ((2.7699*n - 4.3513) - n), citing Alonso & Lamata (2006), and the priority calculator page (ahp-calc.php) displays exactly this value (cr_alo). The same class also contains setSaatyCr() with a classic-style RI table (0.57, 0.9, 1.12, 1.24, 1.32, ...), but that value is not the one the calculator displays. The documented formula is also stated in K. D. Goepel, 'Implementation of an online software tool for the analytic hierarchy process (AHP-OS)', IJAHP 10(3), 2018 (working-paper eq. 2.5). The values given here are the effective RI(n) = (1.7699*n - 4.3513)/(n - 1) implied by the formula; the displayed CRs of all captured matrices reproduce under it (n=7: 0.0220 -> '2.2%'; n=4: 0.0201 -> '2.0%'; n=5: 0.0919 -> '9.2%'). Note this linear-fit variant differs slightly from the Alonso-Lamata Table 1 values used by the fixture ri-table-alonso-lamata (e.g. 0.9094 vs 0.8815 at n=4).

prioritization_method: principal-eigenvector (stated on the results page: 'based on the principal eigenvector'; 'Eigenvector solution' iteration count and delta displayed)

matrices.criteria.priorities.note: Matches the derived expected values at the tool's display precision (percentages to one decimal).

matrices.criteria.lambda_max.note: Tool displays three decimals and iterates to a delta of about 1e-8; tolerance reflects that the displayed value may be rounded or truncated.

matrices.criteria.cr.note: Displayed '2.0%' equals the fixture's published CR 0.02. The tool's linear-fit basis gives 0.0201 and the fixture's Saaty (1980) table gives 0.0204; both display as 2.0%. The Alonso-Lamata Table 1 values would give 0.0208 ('2.1%'), which is how this capture pinned down the tool's CR basis - see ri_table.

matrices.location.cr.note: Displayed '9.2%' equals the fixture's published CR 0.092. The tool's linear-fit basis gives 0.0919 and the fixture's table gives 0.0923, both displaying as 9.2%; the Alonso-Lamata Table 1 values would give 0.0933 ('9.3%').
